nodes.rationale: Service views are native WebContentsViews layered above the shell renderer, so a visible view covers any shell surface. No code path may make one visible while settings, the switcher, or home is on screen — otherwise Home would get the same flash-over treatment Settings did.
nodes.norm_label: overlay invariant: no view visible over a shell surface

nodes.label: homeOpen shell surface
nodes.rationale: Joins switcherOpen and settingsOpen on MainState, ships in the ShellState snapshot, and is never persisted. The renderer keeps deriving (showWelcome = homeOpen || allDisabled), so homeOpen simply gives the all-disabled path a second, user-driven trigger. activeId: ServiceId | null with null meaning home was rejected: it reads well but changes the type of a field threaded through the menu, tray, badges, hibernation and resilience for no behavioral gain.

nodes.label: home:setOpen channel
nodes.rationale: Added to RendererToMain, R2M_CHANNELS and SHELL_ONLY_CHANNELS — it carries no serviceId, so shell-only is the correct classification. Its handler mirrors settings:setOpen: set the flag, hideActive on open and showActive on close, state.touch(), and focus the shell on open so keyboard input reaches it.

nodes.label: anyOverlayOpen
nodes.rationale: A pure predicate over the three surface flags in src/main/lib/overlay-rules.ts, consulted at the call site so ipc-handlers.ts stays thin; resolveActivation is unchanged and only the presentation of its result changes.

nodes.label: views.activate show option
nodes.rationale: With show: false, activate creates the view if needed and moves it to the top of the z-order but leaves it hidden and skips webContents.focus(); showActive() reveals it when the surface closes. That is what makes the invariant enforceable rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: Rail leading sigil
nodes.rationale: A Portal-marked button prepended before the tiles with a hairline divider that keeps it out of the drag-to-reorder run. Head of the rail survives all three railPosition values, which the alternatives did not: a + tile after the last service moves as services are enabled and lands inside the reorder run, and a fourth icon in the bell/gear cluster reads as a setting rather than a place. Tiles gain active={!homeOpen && ...} so none reads as current while Home is up.

nodes.label: Home accelerator (CmdOrCtrl+0)
nodes.rationale: Registered as a menu accelerator rather than a globalShortcut, which is what makes it fire while a service WebContentsView has focus — the mechanism the numbered shortcuts already use. It sits above the service list so the Go menu reads as an ordered index, and it toggles like Cmd/Ctrl K. A plain item, not a checkbox: buildAppMenu rebuilds only on order and disabled changes, so a checkmark would go stale.

nodes.label: activateService clears homeOpen
nodes.rationale: Clearing the flag in the one existing entry point is what makes a rail tile, Cmd/Ctrl 1-6, the quick switcher, and a notification click all leave Home without each learning about it. syncOverlay and win.on('focus') simply grow a third term.

nodes.label: summonDelta
nodes.rationale: Lives in src/shared/welcome.ts beside buildDisabledPatch — process-agnostic and unit-testable — so the confirm button can name the change it is about to apply: "Summon 2 services", "Banish 1 service", "Summon 2 · Banish 1", or "No changes" when the delta is empty.

nodes.label: Seeded, staged picker
nodes.rationale: selected initializes from the live enabled set and re-seeds every time the screen becomes visible, so a discarded edit never survives to the next visit; on a fresh install the enabled set is empty, reproducing the old empty selection exactly. Nothing is written until confirm, and leaving by any other route discards. Banishing the last service is allowed because it produces exactly the fresh-install state on the screen the user is standing on, one click from recovery — blocking it would need a special-case disabled button that reads as a bug.

nodes.label: Escape leaves Home
nodes.rationale: Guarded the way SettingsView guards its own handler: only when Settings and the quick switcher are both closed, and only when at least one service is enabled.

nodes.label: Settings loses the enable toggle
nodes.rationale: Services keeps mute, never-hibernate and reload but lists only enabled services, with a "Manage services…" row that closes Settings and opens Home. This removes the bug class rather than patching it: composition (which services exist) and per-service behavior (how one acts) stop sharing a surface, so the enable toggle no longer lives behind a modal a view can cover.

nodes.label: Persist the surface on change, into Settings
nodes.rationale: Written the moment the surface changes rather than in before-quit, which survives force-quit, a renderer crash, and an OS restart — none of which run before-quit. conf writes synchronously and atomically over a ~1KB file, so a write per switch needs no debounce. A separate session-state store was rejected: a second file to construct, normalize, migrate and test for two scalars that fit an existing one.
nodes.norm_label: persist the surface on change, into settings

nodes.label: Settings.lastActiveId
nodes.rationale: The service focused when the app last closed, defaulting to null. A remembered runtime fact rather than a user preference — lastNotifiedVersion is the precedent.

nodes.label: Settings.lastHomeOpen
nodes.rationale: Records that Home was the surface on top at close — Home is a destination, Settings is a modal you pass through.

nodes.label: Two fields rather than a lastSurface union
nodes.rationale: Home is a layer over a service, not a replacement for one: closing it with Escape must reveal something underneath, so the service identity has to survive independently of whether Home was on top.
nodes.norm_label: two fields rather than a lastsurface union

nodes.label: normalize() leaves lastActiveId intact
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not extended to scrub an unknown lastActiveId: nulling it there would erase the difference between "recorded, but that service is gone" and "never recorded", which the resolver's rules depend on.

nodes.label: resolveStartupSurface
nodes.rationale: One pure resolver in src/main/lib/startup-surface.ts owns the launch surface, joining activation-rules.ts as vitest-covered decision logic so index.ts stays thin wiring. Rules in order: a null record falls back to firstEnabled and honours lastHomeOpen; an enabled recorded id restores; a disabled or catalog-absent id falls back to firstEnabled with homeOpen forced true.

nodes.label: StartupSurface
nodes.rationale: { activeId: ServiceId | null; homeOpen: boolean } — activeId is null only when no service can be activated at all, and homeOpen means Home covers the surface so the view must be activated hidden.

nodes.label: An unrestorable record opens Home, a missing one does not
nodes.rationale: A recorded service now disabled or gone means the app cannot honor the user's last position, so it hands the decision back with the Home picker rather than silently substituting another (user decision, 2026-08-10). But lastActiveId: null is a fresh install or a pre-field upgrade, not a failed restore — treating it as unrestorable would greet every existing user with Home once after upgrading for no information gained. The resolver still falls back to firstEnabled in that row so Escape out of Home lands on a real service.
nodes.norm_label: an unrestorable record opens home, a missing one does not

nodes.label: Startup activates hidden when Home is restored
nodes.rationale: views.activate(surface.activeId, { show: !surface.homeOpen }) is the load-bearing line: a visible view would bury Home exactly the way the settings-modal bug buried Settings. Focus needs no new guard because win.on('focus') and syncOverlay already read the flags set here, before the window finishes loading and the first broadcast fires.
nodes.norm_label: startup activates hidden when home is restored

nodes.label: rememberSurface
nodes.rationale: Writes both fields from live ctx.state rather than taking an id, which makes them impossible to write inconsistently and frees the settings:update call site from reasoning about whether next was applied. Three call sites: activateService, setHomeOpen, and the patch.disabled branch — the last called even when next is null, because that is precisely the unrestorable record that should reopen on Home.

nodes.label: setHomeOpen
nodes.rationale: homeOpen had two writers — the home:setOpen handler and toggleHome in menu.ts — already duplicating the same four steps. Rather than add rememberSurface to both and leave a fifth path free to forget it, the shared part moves into activate.ts. Focus deliberately stays at the call sites: the IPC handler focuses only when opening, toggleHome unconditionally, and collapsing that difference is a behavior change this design does not need.

nodes.label: Nested settings.update inside the handler is safe
nodes.rationale: SettingsStore.update writes through conf directly with no IPC round trip, nothing downstream in the handler reads the two new fields, and the closing ctx.broadcast() re-reads settings.get(). No new IPC channel means nothing to classify in SHELL_ONLY_CHANNELS and no serviceId to validate.
nodes.norm_label: nested settings.update inside the handler is safe

nodes.label: Sections track the live set, the glow tracks the staged set
nodes.rationale: Section membership derives from the live enabled set and the molten face from the staged selection; keeping the two axes independent is the whole design, because a tile you just deselected stays exactly where your cursor left it and only loses its glow. A glowing tile under UNBOUND is the pending-summon signal and a dim tile under SUMMONED the pending-banish signal — no extra ring, dashed border or badge, since the confirm already names the counts. Confirming is the one moment tiles move.
nodes.norm_label: sections track the live set, the glow tracks the staged set

nodes.label: welcomeSections
nodes.rationale: A pure helper joining buildDisabledPatch and summonDelta in src/shared/welcome.ts, partitioning into summoned/unbound in rail order keyed on the LIVE enabled set, never the staged selection, so a tile never moves out from under the cursor mid-edit.

nodes.label: Empty sections keep their headers
nodes.rationale: "Nothing yet." under SUMMONED and "Every one is bound." under UNBOUND. Hiding the empty section was rejected because it would make a fresh install look exactly like the old flat row, so the first-run user never learns the two-section model before they need it. Counts are the tiles below them and change only on confirm — a count that moved while staging would contradict its own tiles. Labels stay Summoned/Unbound in source and are cased by CSS so a screen reader is not spelling out capitals.

nodes.label: Dispel button
nodes.rationale: Discard-in-place: it resets selected to the live enabled set — the same reseed the screen already performs on every visit — because Escape and the rail sigil both discard but also navigate away, so correcting a mis-click meant leaving Home and coming back. It reuses summonLabel's existing disabled flag (true exactly when the delta is empty), so no new predicate and no new test surface. Both buttons go dead together at rest; hiding Dispel when the edit is clean would shift the row's centering on every first click.

nodes.label: PickTile
nodes.rationale: Unchanged by the section split: its `on` prop keeps meaning "is staged on", so all four reachable states fall out of one rule — the face follows selected and nothing else.

nodes.label: Three tip cards that sell three things
nodes.rationale: Two of the three cards were keyboard cheatsheets, so two thirds of the screen's pitch was one idea. Dropping the cheatsheet framing makes room for claims true in code today: Chat only (recipe css plus views.refresh), Stays signed in (partition: persist:${id} per view, so logins survive restarts and no service reads another's cookies), and Quiet & light (ServiceTile badges direct counts and dots indirect traffic, and hibernationMinutes is 30). RailIcon and KeysIcon are deleted for LockIcon and MoonIcon; shortcut discovery survives in the hint line and Settings → Shortcuts.
nodes.norm_label: three tip cards that sell three things

nodes.label: The catalog ships in name order
nodes.rationale: SERVICES and DEFAULT_SETTINGS.order shipped in an ad-hoc order that encodes nothing a user can predict; only the array order changes, since ServiceId's declaration order is meaningless. No migration: normalize() preserves any persisted order, and rewriting a saved order would be the one thing a user cannot undo without redoing it by hand. A services.test.ts invariant asserting the names are localeCompare-sorted keeps the ad-hoc order from coming back.
nodes.norm_label: the catalog ships in name order

nodes.label: summonOrder
nodes.rationale: Newly summoned ids move to the end of order so an arrival lands where the user was last looking rather than jumping into the middle of a rail they have already arranged; a banished id keeps its slot and appends like any other arrival if re-summoned. Several at once append in name order, because selection is a Set carrying no click order and name order is what was on screen. summonDelta is untouched — it returns add in rail order for summonLabel's lengths, and conflating them would couple the button's caption to the ordering rule.

nodes.label: One settings:update patch for disabled + order
nodes.rationale: The existing handler already reads after.order for its teardown loop and for resolveActivation, and buildAppMenu already runs inside the patch.disabled branch keeping Cmd/Ctrl 1-9 aligned. A service:reorder followed by a settings:update would mean two broadcasts and a frame where order and enablement disagree. No new channel — settings:update is already shell-only and order is a key both the handler and normalize() accept.
nodes.norm_label: one settings:update patch for disabled + order

nodes.label: byName
nodes.rationale: Catalog ids in display-name order — the Unbound order and the order new arrivals append in. state.services is settings.order.map(serviceById) and already carries every catalog service with its name, so byName(state.services) needs no new IPC and no new main-process state.

nodes.label: Unbound is always in name order
nodes.rationale: Unbound followed settings.order, so reordering the rail silently reshuffled the pool of services you have not chosen — a list whose order carries no meaning and should therefore never move. The unchosen pool gets a predictable order instead, so the same service is always in the same place however the rail is arranged; Summoned keeps following settings.order because that list is the rail.
nodes.norm_label: unbound is always in name order

nodes.label: matchesQuery
nodes.rationale: Case-insensitive substring on the display name, deliberately not the quick switcher's fuzzyScore: that ranks candidates for a jump-to among a handful of enabled services where a stray match costs one glance, while this filters a visible grid where fuzzyScore("tg") surfacing Instagram beside Telegram reads as a bug and undermines trust in the filter. Results stay in name order with no score re-ranking, so tiles never reorder under the cursor as the query grows. A one-line swap back if substring proves too strict; the unit test pins the choice.

nodes.label: Unbound search control
nodes.rationale: Inline on the Unbound band's label row, right-aligned opposite the count, which costs no vertical height — the whole reason for that placement. Renders only when Unbound is non-empty, clear affordance only while the query is non-empty, aria-label since the band label is not a <label>, and no autofocus: Home is a place, not a modal, and stealing the keyboard on arrival would break Cmd/Ctrl 0 muscle memory and take arrow keys from the tiles. The query resets on every visit and after a confirm, like the selection reseed.

nodes.label: Two-step Escape ladder
nodes.rationale: A non-empty query clears and stops; otherwise Home closes as before. The query is read through a ref rather than an effect dependency so the listener registers once instead of on every keystroke and never closes over a stale value. Handling it on the input's own onKeyDown was rejected: stopping a React synthetic event from reaching a native window listener is a bug waiting to happen, and it would leave Escape closing Home while a filter is active whenever focus sits elsewhere.

nodes.label: Drag-to-reorder on Home
nodes.rationale: Reordering was only reachable from the rail — the one surface covered while Home is open. Summoned tiles mirror ServiceTile exactly and persist immediately through the existing service:reorder channel: reordering is non-destructive, so there is nothing to confirm and Summon/Dispel keep meaning enable/disable only. The rail visibly re-ordering behind Home is the confirmation. Unbound tiles are not draggable — that section has no order to edit.

nodes.label: moveTo
nodes.rationale: The rail's inline index arithmetic extracted to a tested helper rather than copied to a second surface. Splice semantics are preserved verbatim including the index-shift quirk (to is resolved before the removal, so a forward move lands one slot short) — the extraction adds a test, not a fix. Both surfaces reorder the full settings.order and the disabled ids between the endpoints ride along, exactly as on the rail today.

nodes.label: Board layout (header / bands / pinned footer)
nodes.rationale: Three directions were measured in a real Chromium layout pass, not estimated: at 8 services all three fit the 748px budget, but at a Ferdium-sized 62 services the compact column wants 1040px and the two-column split 852px, while the board's home area scrollHeight still equals its clientHeight. The board wins because no-scrolling is a property of the layout rather than a coincidence of content — only the tile areas grow, and they grow into their own scroll containers. The header and action bar never move, so the confirm is always on screen instead of being the first thing to fall off the bottom. Width was never the constraint, which is why the split gains nothing at scale.

nodes.label: Two states, one skeleton
nodes.rationale: On a fresh install the compact header is replaced by the welcome block (portal, title, tagline, tip cards) and the single band reads "Choose your services"; once anything is summoned the tips give their space back and the Summoned band appears. The tips are onboarding — they earn their space exactly once, and reclaiming it is what gives the steady state room while showing more tiles.

nodes.label: Board sizing rules
nodes.rationale: The board is flex-1 min-h-0 under an already-definite height chain so a percentage cap resolves; Summoned is capped at max-h-[46%] because without it a long summoned list crowds Unbound out of the board entirely; Unbound is flex-[0_1_auto] so it shrinks rather than pushing the footer; each band's tile area is the scroll container so its scrollHeight is the honest measure. Tile labels truncate to one line — a two-line label pushes its whole row taller and breaks the grid. The first-run stack centers with margin: auto, the standing fix for justify-center plus overflow-y-auto clipping the top of overflowing content instead of scrolling to it (a latent bug in today's screen).

nodes.label: welcome/ServiceBand.tsx
nodes.rationale: Label row, optional aside slot, scroll area, empty state. Keeps the welcome-section-summoned/-unbound testids so existing e2e selectors survive; on a fresh install the single "Choose your services" band carries welcome-section-unbound because it is the unbound band relabelled, so selectors need not know which state they are in.

nodes.label: welcome/WelcomeIntro.tsx
nodes.rationale: Portal, title, tagline and tip cards, first run only, carrying data-testid="welcome-intro" — the hook that replaces welcome.spec.ts's "Nothing yet." assertion, since the first-run state has no Summoned band.

nodes.label: The rail overflows before Home does
nodes.rationale: At 32px per tile plus a 6px gap, roughly 30 summoned services fill a 1280px rail and the rest fall off the end. Home survives 62 services in this design; the rail does not survive summoning them — a separate change. Compact 48px unlabelled tiles roughly halve the height cost and are the obvious next lever past ~150 services, so they are not built now.
nodes.norm_label: the rail overflows before home does

nodes.label: Instagram chat service
nodes.rationale: The eighth service: id instagram, url https://www.instagram.com/direct/inbox/ (the chat surface directly, never the feed), colour #E4405F, waitForReady: true, placed after messenger and shipping disabled. Like facebook.com the site is mostly not chat — feed, reels, explore, profiles — so it needs the full chat-only treatment.

nodes.label: normalize() catalog-position slotting
nodes.rationale: Ids missing from a persisted order slot in at their catalog position — right after the nearest catalog predecessor the user already has — rather than appending, so instagram lands beside messenger on existing installs too. Revised the same day after a live smoke test showed it appended to the end of the rail.

nodes.label: chatPaths: ['/direct']
nodes.rationale: Covers /direct/inbox/ and /direct/t/<thread>. Login flows at /accounts/login/ never reach a chat path, so they are never snapped back.

nodes.label: meta-unread.ts shared Meta heuristics
nodes.rationale: Instagram web shares Meta's chat-list DOM language with facebook.com/messages — bold text, a small blue dot, an "Unread" screen-reader string — so messenger's unread-row detection and banner-text extraction move verbatim into a shared module parameterized by thread-link selector and a link-to-row resolver. Messenger keeps [role='row']; instagram resolves [role='listitem'], [role='row'] with the link itself as fallback. Messenger's behavior is unchanged and its existing fixture tests are the proof.

nodes.label: Instagram synthNotification
nodes.rationale: Instagram DMs never notify in-page — delegated to browser push, which Electron cannot receive — so sender and preview come from the first unread row's dir="auto" spans with the time suffix stripped, mirroring messenger's.

nodes.label: hideChrome recipe hook
nodes.rationale: An optional hook returning Element[], run by the runner every tick with an idempotent display:none inside try/catch so SPA re-renders get re-hidden. Introduced because two live smoke tests showed no static selector survives for Instagram's nav rail: it is hash-classed, half its icons are role=button, and it carries no nav/role=navigation landmark. A throw must never break counting.

nodes.label: Structural nav-rail computation
nodes.rationale: The rail is computed as the branch holding the DM nav link (one not inside main) that sits beside main. Login pages render no main, so they are untouched, and a layout that nests the nav inside main hides nothing rather than risking the chat surface — failing closed on the surface that matters.

nodes.label: Rail space reclaim
nodes.rationale: Because the rail is position:fixed, hiding it leaves its reserved width as a dead column in two shapes. So hideChrome also walks main up to the layout root inclusive plus the single-child wrapper spine below main, zeroing any rail-sized (>=40px) left margin/padding/offset — pane-internal paddings are far smaller and survive — and stretching any element under-filling its parent by >=40px, which is the width: calc(100% - rail) leftover that otherwise strands a blank strip at the pane's right edge.

nodes.label: StyleX atomic class .x132t2bv
nodes.rationale: A live inspection found this padded wrapper (padding-inline-start: 72px) outside the original ancestor chain. The recipe css zeroes its padding directly because StyleX hashes are derived from the single declaration they carry and so survive rebuilds far better than component classes, with the structural reclaim as the fallback if the hash ever rotates.

nodes.label: pointer-events inerting of off-chat links
nodes.rationale: pointer-events: none on a[href^='/']:not([href^='/direct']) — thread-header avatar and username, @mentions, shared posts — instead of letting them navigate and then snap back. Messenger gains the same inert rule for its profile links, both gated on the chat surface being mounted so login and captcha pages stay untouched.

nodes.label: Instagram calibration caveat
nodes.rationale: Selectors follow Meta's messenger DOM language but are uncalibrated against a live logged-in session (tiktok precedent), noted in the recipe until a live login pass; ALLOWED_HOSTS verification needs the same session.

nodes.label: ALLOWED_HOSTS.instagram
nodes.rationale: www.instagram.com, instagram.com, accounts.instagram.com, plus www.facebook.com/facebook.com for the Log-in-with-Facebook bounce. VERIFY LIVE before wiring enforcement.

nodes.label: macOS copy-cursor badge defect
nodes.rationale: Neither tile surface set effectAllowed or dropEffect, so Chromium fell back to copy — drawn by macOS as a green ⊕ badge faded in on the window server's schedule, a beat behind the pointer. Semantically wrong for a reorder and the slowest-updating thing on screen. Worse, no dragenter/dragleave/dragend handlers existed on either tile, so order changed only at drop: the OS badge was the sole moving element, which is exactly why the gesture read as laggy. Setting both effects to move removes the badge but leaves the gesture silent rather than slow.

nodes.label: Reorder.Group / pointer-driven reorder
nodes.rationale: motion's Reorder.Group/Item replace the HTML5 handlers on both tiles, in devDependencies since electron-vite bundles the renderer and it is never in the packaged node_modules. With no OS drag session there is no OS cursor to lag: the tile under the pointer is the real tile transformed at frame rate, and the neighbours animating into the vacated slot make the resulting order self-evident before release — an insertion line describes the outcome, a live gap is the outcome. Axis detection from item positions supports Home's wrapping grid, the one property that could have disqualified the direction; draggable, onDragStart/onDragOver/onDrop and the text/goetia-service data type are deleted. cursor-grab/grabbing survives and now holds for the whole gesture.

nodes.label: Draft order, committed once on drag end
nodes.rationale: Reorder.Group is controlled and fires onReorder on every crossing, not on release — wired straight to service:reorder, one drag across three tiles would be three conf writes, three MainState broadcasts, three rail re-renders and three app-menu rebuilds, the per-tick broadcast CLAUDE.md forbids. So the drag runs entirely in the renderer and reaches main once, sending `shown` rather than `draft` so a drag ending where it started is a harmless no-op instead of a crash on null. The draft is cleared when the broadcast carrying the new order arrives, not on commit — clearing on commit would render one frame of the pre-drag order during the round trip, a visible snap-back exactly when the drop should have taken. Since the arriving order equals the draft, clearing is visually a no-op, and any other mid-drag order change trips the same condition and drops the draft rather than letting a stale local array fight broadcast state.
nodes.norm_label: draft order, committed once on drag end

nodes.label: applySubsetOrder
nodes.rationale: Reorder.Group knows only the ids it renders while settings.order holds the whole catalog including disabled ids, and moveTo's (from, to) signature cannot express merging a finished array back in. The `known` filter is not decoration: without it an unknown id still enters the slots set and shifts the cursor, so full=[A,B,C], subset=[Z,C,A] yields [Z,B,C]; filtering first makes matching slots equal moved.length exactly. Deliberate behaviour change — moveTo spliced the full array so disabled ids between endpoints rode along, while this pins every non-member to its absolute index; the old behaviour was an implementation side effect, and a hidden id shifting because of a visible drag is unobservable and cannot be reasoned about from the screen.

nodes.label: Rail Reorder.Group wiring
nodes.rationale: The <nav> also holds the Home button, a divider and the bell/gear cluster, but Reorder.Group measures its own children to detect axis and compute crossings — so the tiles move into their own flex box, which becomes the group, keeping the same gap and alignment so the rendered result is unchanged. axis is set explicitly rather than detected because a rail holding a single service has no second item to infer from; Home's grid needs axis="xy" because it wraps and a tile dragged to another row moves on both axes.

nodes.label: Transform ownership (Motion vs Tailwind scale)
nodes.rationale: ServiceTile's scale-105 sits on the very button that becomes the Reorder.Item, and Motion writes transform on the element it drags, so Tailwind's scale and Motion's translate would overwrite each other. The active scale moves into Motion's hands as animate={{ scale }} and scale-105 leaves stateClasses. PickTile needs no equivalent change: its scale-105 is on the inner face span.

nodes.label: Trailing-click guard
nodes.rationale: HTML5 drag-and-drop suppressed the click that follows a completed drag; pointer drag does not, so releasing on Home would toggle that service off and on the rail would activate it — a drag that silently performs the tile's click action is worse than the lag being fixed. onDragStart sets a ref that onClick consumes and clears before the tile's own handler runs, and Motion fires onDragStart only past its drag threshold, so an ordinary click never sets it.

nodes.label: layoutScroll on the scrolling band
nodes.rationale: Motion's projection needs layoutScroll on a scrollable ancestor to correct for scroll offset; without it a drag inside a scrolled Summoned band computes crossings against stale rects. It only bites once Summoned overflows its max-h-[46%], which is why it is easy to ship broken.

nodes.label: Order-insensitive enabledKey
nodes.rationale: enabledKey joined the enabled ids in settings.order, so it was order-sensitive and a reorder changed it without changing the enabled set — dropping a tile on Home therefore discarded whatever the user had staged for Summon and cleared the search box. The reseed is about membership, not order (its own comment says so), so sorting before joining makes the key say that; the consumer splits it back into a Set, so sorted order is immaterial. A summon, dispel or catalog change still trips it; a pure reorder no longer does. Shipping a pleasant reorder onto a reorder that eats staged work would make the bug more reachable, not less.

nodes.label: What the drag looks like
nodes.rationale: whileDrag scale 1.1 plus a raised shadow, neighbours settling on Motion's default spring; badge, mute, crash and stale decorations ride along as the tile's children and the on/active gradient is untouched. No landing pulse and no band hint — the reflow is the confirmation, and the rail reordering behind Home is the second one.

nodes.label: Pointer drag makes the reorder path e2e-testable
nodes.rationale: Pointer-driven drag is reachable from mouse.down/move/up, which HTML5 drag-and-drop never was — so the renderer → service:reorder → main → broadcast path can be covered end to end for the first time, which is the e2e-on-wiring the definition of done asks for.
nodes.norm_label: pointer drag makes the reorder path e2e-testable

nodes.label: Slack recipe fixture
nodes.rationale: The count oracle for the slack recipe, with the sidebar mounted (.p-channel_sidebar plus data-qa="workspace_sidebar") so ready() is true; the title "Slack - Goetia HQ" carries no (n), so the badge path rather than the title fallback is what is measured.

nodes.label: Mention-badge rows (2 + 1 → direct 3)
nodes.rationale: alice and bob are unread rows carrying .c-mention_badge values that sum to the direct count, and being badge-bearing they must be excluded from indirect so a mentioned channel is not counted twice.

nodes.label: Badge-less unread channels (indirect 2)
nodes.rationale: general and launch are unread with no badge, which is exactly the indirect signal; the read #archive row anchors the negative case.

nodes.label: Muted unread row that counts nothing
nodes.rationale: #noise carries both --unread and --muted, pinning the :not(--muted) half of the indirect selector.
nodes.norm_label: muted unread row that counts nothing

nodes.label: Tagline: Summon every chat to one window, nothing but the chat
nodes.norm_label: tagline: summon every chat to one window, nothing but the chat

nodes.label: Ember Gradient Palette (arcA, arcB, core, word)
nodes.norm_label: ember gradient palette (arca, arcb, core, word)

nodes.label: Flat White Camera Glyph on Crimson Squircle
nodes.norm_label: flat white camera glyph on crimson squircle

nodes.label: Branded Squircle Tile Notification Icon Convention
nodes.norm_label: branded squircle tile notification icon convention

nodes.label: Slack Octothorpe Brand Mark (white on aubergine)
nodes.norm_label: slack octothorpe brand mark (white on aubergine)

nodes.label: electronFuses block
nodes.rationale: Locks the packaged binary: no run-as-node/NODE_OPTIONS/--inspect code-exec paths, cookies encrypted via OS keychain rather than plaintext SQLite, and the asar integrity-checked as the only load source. Flipping fuses invalidates the signature, so resetAdHocDarwinSignature re-applies the ad-hoc identity.

nodes.label: Ad-hoc mac signing identity '-'
nodes.rationale: macOS refuses Notification Center registration for unsigned bundles — notifications fail with UNErrorDomain 1 and no permission prompt — so the build is ad-hoc signed even though it isn't notarized.

nodes.label: Custom hardened-runtime entitlements
nodes.rationale: Not electron-builder's default set: grants only the JIT and library-validation exceptions Chromium needs to launch ad-hoc under the hardened runtime, without allow-dyld-environment-variables.

nodes.label: Mic/camera usage descriptions in extendInfo
nodes.rationale: macOS refuses mic/camera access without usage descriptions in Info.plist.

nodes.label: Notification icons shipped unpacked
nodes.rationale: The OS opens these paths itself, so they must be real files rather than asar entries.

nodes.label: Service Back Affordance Implementation Plan (reverted)
nodes.rationale: Status 2026-08-13: partially reverted, do not execute. Task 1 (firstRunUrl teardown) shipped and stands; Tasks 2–7 were implemented, verified green, then removed the same day on the user's decision. Kept as the execution record.

nodes.label: backAvailable predicate
nodes.rationale: One pure predicate: back is offered only when the view has history AND is on a host other than the service's own. Its answer rides ServiceRuntime.backAvailable through the existing report-on-change broadcast; views.goBack stays dumb so the menu item behaves like browser back while the contextual surfaces are the gated ones.

nodes.label: firstRunUrl mechanism removal
nodes.rationale: A pure deletion with no red-green cycle to fake: typecheck enumerates every referencing site and the existing suite proves no behavior was lost. Slack was the only consumer and Settings.visited existed solely to serve it.

nodes.label: Home Redesign and Summon Cap Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Cap summoned services at 9 (the accelerator ceiling), replace Home's two layouts with one split-console screen, and move Summon/Discard into the hero where they are always in reach.
nodes.norm_label: home redesign and summon cap implementation plan

nodes.label: MAX_SUMMONED / capBlocked / trimToCap
nodes.rationale: MAX_SUMMONED must equal MAX_SERVICE_ACCELERATORS (9), locked by a unit test. No new IPC channel: settings:update already carries disabled+order, and SettingsStore.normalize is the cap's single enforcement point, persisting a one-time boot trim surfaced as ShellState.capTrimmed.

nodes.label: HomeHero + SummonGauge single layout
nodes.rationale: Welcome recomposes into HomeHero (portal, gauge, actions) beside the two ServiceBands, deleting WelcomeIntro and the 'fresh' branch — one screen for every state instead of two layouts.

nodes.label: Reload Guard Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Drop user-initiated reloads that would interrupt a wake already in flight, and remove the per-service reload button from Settings ▸ Services.

nodes.label: reload-guard predicate (RELOAD_MIN_INTERVAL_MS)
nodes.rationale: A pure predicate over the waking flag and the last accepted reload timestamp, consulted at ServiceViewManager.refresh — the single choke point every user reload path reaches. views.reload stays unguarded because crash recovery has its own backoff and five-reload cap. A dropped reload produces no toast, dialog, sound or log line: the overlay already reads 'Waking X…' for the whole blocked interval.

nodes.label: Service-View Context Menu Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Right-click inside a service view pops a native menu: spelling fixes, clipboard editing, and gated hand-offs for links and images.

nodes.label: buildContextMenuTemplate pure builder
nodes.rationale: Turns a narrow projection of Electron's context-menu params into plain-data descriptors so the matrix is unit-testable; views.ts stays wiring. The isSafeExternalUrl gate for open-link descriptors lives inside the builder, not the wiring, so it cannot be bypassed. No new IPC channel and no destroy() change — the listener rides the view's own webContents lifetime.

nodes.label: Calls and Screen Share Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Voice/video calls and screen sharing work wherever the service's web client supports them: call popups open as hardened in-app windows, device permissions reach call surfaces, the packaged mac app can access mic/camera, and getDisplayMedia gets the native picker.
nodes.norm_label: calls and screen share implementation plan

nodes.label: call-policy (CALL_POPUPS, CALL_ORIGINS, isCallPopup)
nodes.rationale: Deny stays the default for window.open: only isCallPopup URLs may return action:'allow', and child windows get their own deny-all handler plus isNavigationAllowed confinement. Call windows override to contextIsolation+sandbox true — harder than the service view, never softer. notifications never extends beyond the service origin; only media and display-capture may use CALL_ORIGINS.

nodes.label: setDisplayMediaRequestHandler with useSystemPicker
nodes.rationale: Per-session handler with a fallback so screen share gets the OS-native picker rather than a hand-rolled source list.

nodes.label: Light Sleep Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Hibernated services keep badges and notifications working via periodic hidden peeks, so all services can sleep by default and the app stays light without going blind. neverHibernate defaults flip to false now that sleeping is safe.

nodes.label: peek-rules scheduling helper
nodes.rationale: A pure helper decides which sleeping service is due; HibernationController absorbs the peek cycle into its existing 60s sweep rather than owning a second timer.

nodes.label: ctx.noteUnreadReport late-bound hook
nodes.rationale: Signals peek completion from the unread:* IPC handlers, mirroring noteActivated — so the peek ends on real evidence rather than a fixed sleep, with a timeout as the backstop. Late binding keeps hibernation.ts free of electron.

nodes.label: Quiet Hours Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: A daily start–end window with per-day toggles silences Goetia like global mute does, with a manual unmute dismissing exactly the current window.

nodes.label: quiet-hours-rules (quietWindowFor, quietNow, nextBoundary, muteToggleResult)
nodes.rationale: Times are HH:MM 24h local; days indexed by Date.getDay() with 0 = Sunday; a crossing window belongs to the day it starts; start === end is an empty window. Engagement is computed from the wall clock, never persisted — the only persisted quiet state is the schedule and quietOverrideWindowStart.

nodes.label: QuietHoursController one-timer boundary
nodes.rationale: One setTimeout re-armed on fire and on schedule edits, cleared in dispose() on before-quit — the bounded-timers rule rather than a polling interval. No new IPC channel: quietHours rides settings:update and quietActive rides shell:state.

nodes.label: Summon Hotkey Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: A system-wide shortcut (curated combos, default Alt+CmdOrCtrl+G, off by default) shows or hides Goetia from any app, with failed registrations surfaced in Settings.

nodes.label: SUMMON_COMBOS curated accelerator list
nodes.rationale: A curated list rather than free-form capture: the persisted accelerator must always be one of SUMMON_COMBOS, enforced by normalize(). Status rides MainState.summonHotkeyOk on the existing broadcast, and the registration is torn down in dispose() from the existing before-quit block.

nodes.label: Banner → Exact Conversation Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Clicking a banner lands the user in the conversation that fired it — lane A replays the site's own notification onclick, lane B navigates to the thread href a synthetic recipe already held — with every failure mode degrading to today's activate-the-service behavior.

nodes.label: resolveBannerClick decision (show / activate / navigate / replay)
nodes.rationale: Goetia never learns a service's conversation DOM: main holds only the pure validation rule, while routing knowledge stays in the page (lane A) or the recipe's existing row anchor (lane B).

nodes.label: Notification shim click registry + replay handle
nodes.rationale: The shim keeps each page Notification in a capped registry and returns a replay handle; notification:fired carries clickId/href, and the only new IPC surface is the main→service-view notification:replayClick.
nodes.norm_label: notification shim click registry + replay handle

nodes.label: BANNER_GRACE_MS peek grace
nodes.rationale: A 2-minute grace in HibernationController stops Light Sleep destroying a peek view before its banner can be clicked — otherwise the replay target dies between the banner and the click.

nodes.label: v0.9 Zoom, Sign-Out, and Quick-Switcher Recents Plan
nodes.rationale: Three independent slices: per-service zoom (Home moves to ⌘⇧H so ⌘0 can become Actual Size), a rail-tile menu with local sign-out, and a Recent-conversations section fed by an in-memory activity log.
nodes.norm_label: v0.9 zoom, sign-out, and quick-switcher recents plan

nodes.label: zoom-rules (clampZoom, stepZoom)
nodes.rationale: Zoom levels use Chromium's 1.2^level scale: step 0.5, clamp [-3.5, 3.5], default 0. Persisted per service.

nodes.label: activity-log (in-memory recents)
nodes.rationale: Lives only in main memory, fed by the already-throttled banner stream, and crosses IPC as display fields plus opaque ids — hrefs never leave main and clicks re-validate through resolveBannerClick. New channels service:tileMenu, activity:open (send) and activity:recent (invoke) are all shell-only.

nodes.label: switcher-results ranking
nodes.rationale: Pure result rules so the switcher can merge services and recent conversations without a per-banner broadcast — it fetches recents once per open.

nodes.label: Auto-Banish Unused Services Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Opt-in auto-banish of services unused for N hours (default 24), plus consolidation of all sleep-related settings into the Services pane.

nodes.label: shouldBanish pure rule
nodes.rationale: Takes a BanishCandidate (disabled, active, neverHibernate, peeking, lastUsedAt) plus now and banishMs; BANISH_MIN_HOURS 1, BANISH_MAX_HOURS 720. Mirrors hibernation-rules in shape so the sweep can evaluate both.

nodes.label: lastUsedAt activation clock
nodes.rationale: Stamped only on activation, riding the existing rememberSurface write so there is one settings write per action. Banners, badges, unread reports and peeks never touch it — otherwise a service you never open would look used.

nodes.label: applyDisabledChange + ctx.banishServices
nodes.rationale: The shared side-effects tail Home's banish already uses, reached from the sweep via a late-bound ctx.banishServices — applyDisabledChange lives in ipc-handlers.ts so hibernation.ts and activate.ts stay importable by unit tests without loading electron. A banish batch is one patch.

nodes.label: Home Board ↔ Rail Reorder Sync Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: A rail drag while Home is open syncs a clean board silently (no spurious 'Apply new order'), and asks before discarding a dirty board's staged edit. Renderer-only coordination through two zustand fields — no main-process or IPC changes.
nodes.norm_label: home board ↔ rail reorder sync implementation plan

nodes.label: followLiveOrder helper
nodes.rationale: Compares the staged order against the comma-join of the live summoned order the board last saw: a clean board returns a copy of the new live order, a dirty board returns staged unchanged by the same reference so React skips the re-render.

nodes.label: RailReorderPrompt commit intercept
nodes.rationale: useTileReorder gains an optional commit intercept plus cancelDraft(); the Rail holds the drop behind a confirm when the board is dirty. The intercept defers the single send rather than adding another, so reorder still reaches IPC at most once per drag.

nodes.label: Login Purge Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Rename the per-service Sign out… to Purge login… in red, and add a Home-wide Purge all logins… sweep that reaches every service including unbound ones.

nodes.label: purgeService shared wipe unit
nodes.rationale: src/main/signout.ts becomes src/main/purge.ts with one shared unit both entry points call. The bulk path iterates settings.order behind a confirm and returns a count over a new invoke channel (services:purgeAll), so the completion toast never touches ShellState. Purge must never touch disabled or order.

nodes.label: --danger design token
nodes.rationale: Red gets its own token (#d1293d light, #ff5a6a dark, exposed as --color-danger) rather than reusing --badge (unread) or --accent-2 (the hero gradient's end stop), which mean different things.

nodes.label: Sign-Out in Settings, Tile Banish Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Move Sign Out… from the rail tile's right-click menu into Settings → Services, and put a quick no-confirm Banish in its tile-menu slot.
nodes.norm_label: sign-out in settings, tile banish implementation plan

nodes.label: service:signOut shell-only channel
nodes.rationale: Shell-only because a service page must never be able to trigger a partition wipe, its own included. confirmSignOut stays byte-identical: native confirm defaulting to Cancel, call windows closed, persist:<id> cleared, view reloaded to the chat URL.

nodes.label: Tile-menu Banish (no confirm)
nodes.rationale: No confirm dialog because it is quick and fully recoverable — the login is kept and the service re-summons on Home. Sign-out keeps its confirm because it destroys credentials. It reuses ctx.banishServices([id]).

nodes.label: Slack service (ninth service)
nodes.rationale: Whole app.slack.com/client surface is chat (Discord precedent), so no chatPaths are needed; cosmetic CSS hiding is the entire chat-only treatment. Workspace-scoped client means no per-workspace configuration in Goetia.

nodes.label: Slack recipe count()
nodes.rationale: One querySelectorAll pass scoped to the sidebar; direct = mention badges with unreadFromTitle fallback, indirect = unread non-muted badge-less channel rows so a mentioned channel is never double-counted. No layout reads, no store access, settles synchronously — the 24/7 cost rule.

nodes.label: Slack recipe ready()
nodes.rationale: visiblyPresent on the channel sidebar; Slack's 'loading your workspace' splash is long, so the waking cover earns its keep.

nodes.label: Slack chat-only CSS
nodes.rationale: Discord-level hiding of Upgrade/Pro CTAs, get-the-app banners, and Canvases/Files/Automations/Templates entries; Home, DMs, Activity, threads and the workspace switcher stay because that is chat. Gated on the chat surface being mounted so login pages stay untouched.

nodes.label: firstRunUrl and lib/start-url.ts (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Original decision: the first creation of the Slack view loads a workspace-agnostic entry URL because logged-out /client 302s to a workspace-first signin that assumes the user knows a workspace URL. Superseded 2026-08-13 — firstRunUrl, Settings.visited and lib/start-url.ts were torn down; every service starts on url and reload is the escape.

nodes.label: Slack ALLOWED_HOSTS entry
nodes.rationale: app.slack.com, slack.com, www.slack.com. Two live-pass gaps flagged: per-user workspace hosts ({team}.slack.com) that exact-host matching cannot express, and SSO bounce hosts (Google/Apple).

nodes.label: No back affordance — reload is the only way back
nodes.rationale: Built in full, verified green and against live Slack, then rejected the same day: back is browser chrome, Goetia is a chat shell not a browser, and reload already lands on the chat URL — a second history-shaped way back buys discoverability at the price of the product's premise. Do not re-propose without a new decision.
nodes.norm_label: no back affordance — reload is the only way back

nodes.label: back-affordance.ts off-chat predicate (removed)
nodes.rationale: Gated on host plus first path segment of SERVICES[].url. The first implementation compared host only, which meant it never fired on the one trap it existed for while 356 unit tests and 18 e2e specs stayed green — unit tests only prove a predicate matches the URLs you imagined.

nodes.label: Slack logged-out flow stays on app.slack.com
nodes.rationale: Driving the built app showed the 302 lands on app.slack.com/workspace-signin and 'Find your workspaces' on app.slack.com/get-started#/find — only the path changes. A redirect's host AND path are part of a service's contract and belong in its spec; live-URL assumptions are verified by driving the built app, not by reasoning from an earlier doc.
nodes.norm_label: slack logged-out flow stays on app.slack.com

nodes.label: MAX_SUMMONED cap of 9
nodes.rationale: The cap exists because service accelerators stop at Cmd/Ctrl 9 (MAX_SERVICE_ACCELERATORS); a unit test asserts the two constants never drift. Evaluated against the staged result live in the picker, not at confirm time; the catalog keeps all 10 services and can grow.

nodes.label: trimToCap and normalize() enforcement
nodes.rationale: normalize() enforces enabled<=9 on every read so rail, app menu, quick switcher and activation never see a 10th enabled service — main-process normalize is the enforcement point, so a hostile renderer payload cannot exceed the cap. Overflow is every enabled id past the 9th position in settings.order; a boot trim persists once and rides ShellState.capTrimmed into a self-dismissing toast.

nodes.label: capBlocked picker rule
nodes.rationale: At the cap every unpicked tile renders dimmed and disabled while picked tiles stay clickable, so unpicking one re-enables the rest within the same edit.

nodes.label: HomeHero fixed left column
nodes.rationale: One layout for every state replaces the fresh/steady branch: the wow of the first-run intro is spent once and every layout change had to be designed twice. WelcomeIntro.tsx is deleted and the pitch becomes permanent furniture as bottom micro-copy.

nodes.label: SummonGauge ring
nodes.rationale: Purely presentational SVG ring taking {staged, cap, dirty}; the fill fraction is staged/cap — the number the user is about to have, not the live one. All hero animation is CSS in the shell renderer: no recipe cost, no JS timers, nothing to clean up.

nodes.label: Discard replaces Dispel
nodes.rationale: 'Dispel' read like 'banish my services' when it actually discards a staged edit; Discard renders only when a staged change exists, chosen over an always-visible reset and a destructive Dispel-all.

nodes.label: reloadAllowed reload guard
nodes.rationale: Two arms, neither redundant: waking is the semantically right signal (the same flag the overlay renders), and RELOAD_MIN_INTERVAL_MS covers the race the flag cannot — waking turns true asynchronously from did-start-navigation while F5 auto-repeat lands ~30 reloads per second inside that window. Guarding views.refresh covers all four reload paths at one choke point.

nodes.label: Why the reload guard cannot trap the user
nodes.rationale: The wake self-expires at WAKE_TIMEOUT_MS (10s) regardless of the page, and onCrashed calls waking.end before the Retry placeholder renders so crash Retry is never blocked by the waking arm. A dropped reload gets no new feedback — the 'Waking X…' overlay already answers 'why did nothing happen'.
nodes.norm_label: why the reload guard cannot trap the user

nodes.label: views.reload stays unguarded
nodes.rationale: Crash recovery's current-URL reload is not user-initiated and already has backoff and a five-reload cap; routing it through a floor meant for keystrokes would only fight its own schedule.

nodes.label: Settings loses its per-service reload button
nodes.rationale: It duplicated Cmd+R for the active service and, for an inactive one, reloaded a page the user cannot see. The service:reload channel and its shell-only classification stay because the crashed-view placeholder's Retry still needs them.
nodes.norm_label: settings loses its per-service reload button

nodes.label: Service-view native context menu
nodes.rationale: Views ship spellcheck but no context-menu listener existed, so a suggestion could never be accepted and mouse-driven copy/paste did not exist. Scope 'essentials + hand-offs' chosen over clipboard-only and full browser-style: Look Up and Search with Google each add a non-chat hand-off Goetia does not otherwise have. The page's own menu always wins because Electron only emits context-menu when the DOM event was not preventDefault-ed.

nodes.label: buildContextMenuTemplate
nodes.rationale: Pure decision matrix in src/main/lib/context-menu.ts while views.ts stays wiring; it imports isSafeExternalUrl from the neighbouring external-url.ts so the link gate sits inside the tested unit. copy-link appears for any linkURL (copying an address is inert) while open-link additionally requires isSafeExternalUrl. An empty result means the wiring must not pop a menu.

nodes.label: Open Link in Browser hand-off
nodes.rationale: The same hand-off the window-open handler already gives target=_blank links, extended to same-tab links so a left-click no longer walks the view off chat and leans on snapback or reload to recover.

nodes.label: Add to Dictionary is per service
nodes.rationale: Custom words live in the persist:<id> session like cookies, so a word added in WhatsApp still squiggles in Telegram. That matches the isolation story and is not worth cross-session plumbing.
nodes.norm_label: add to dictionary is per service

nodes.label: call-policy.ts (CALL_POPUPS / CALL_ORIGINS / isCallPopup)
nodes.rationale: Per-service call-popup patterns (host + pathPrefix, https only) and call-capable sibling origins, seeded from known web-client behaviour with the same VERIFY-LIVE caveat as ALLOWED_HOSTS. A deliberate narrow amendment to the deny-by-default external-links rule: a call is chat, and the window is confined.

nodes.label: Inert guest popup (never commits a navigation)
nodes.rationale: Two facts invalidated both prior containment designs: an about:blank popup's webPreferences cannot be overridden (Chromium skips browser-side navigation for blank popups), so the 'hardened' override never applied; and a same-process guest that commits a navigation crashes the shared renderer whenever the opener's Node env has work pending (electron#36858 class, reproduced as SIGSEGV exit 11). The guest opens hidden, keeps the page's scriptable window.open contract alive, and will-navigate is always prevented.
nodes.norm_label: inert guest popup (never commits a navigation)

nodes.label: Call URL adoption into a hardened call window
nodes.rationale: A guest navigation to an isCallPopup URL is adopted into a standalone window with contextIsolation + sandbox on, no preload, no opener, same persist:<id> partition so the signed-in session and session-level permission/display-media handlers apply. Its own navigations must pass isCallPopup or isNavigationAllowed or it closes; popups from it are denied; call windows close on service destroy but never on service switch — a call outlives the surface that placed it.
nodes.norm_label: call url adoption into a hardened call window

nodes.label: isBlankCallPopup (about:blank popups)
nodes.rationale: The live pass showed Messenger opens its call popup as about:blank and script-navigates it, so an https-only matcher can never admit it — the missing permission prompt was purely downstream of the popup never opening. Blank popups are admitted only for services whose CALL_POPUPS list is non-empty, which stays the marker that a service has calls at all.

nodes.label: macOS call entitlements and usage descriptions
nodes.rationale: hardenedRuntime with no device.audio-input/.camera entitlement and no NSMicrophone/NSCameraUsageDescription made getUserMedia fail in the packaged build even for in-page callers; dev appeared to work only because the stock Electron binary ships its own usage descriptions. The prohibition on allow-dyld-environment-variables is untouched.
nodes.norm_label: macos call entitlements and usage descriptions

nodes.label: setDisplayMediaRequestHandler with the system picker
nodes.rationale: useSystemPicker means macOS 15+ draws its own screen/window picker and Goetia draws nothing; the fallback grants the primary screen via desktopCapturer rather than failing the request. Session-level registration covers call popups automatically. A custom picker UI is explicitly deferred.

nodes.label: permissionAllowed gains call origins
nodes.rationale: media and display-capture are granted on the service origin or any of the service's CALL_ORIGINS, while notifications stay strictly origin-exact. display-capture was not in the allowlist at all, so screen share was denied before any picker could run. Malformed URLs and unlisted permissions stay denied.

nodes.label: Light Sleep (peek while hibernated)
nodes.rationale: No aggregator offers hibernation preserving both session and awareness — Ferdium logs services out on wake, Franz and Rambox go blind, Beeper's bridging breaks when platforms change. Goetia already preserves sessions via persist:<id>; Light Sleep adds awareness so a badge is at most one peek interval stale instead of frozen forever.

nodes.label: peek-rules.ts scheduling
nodes.rationale: Pure logic in lib/ with HibernationController absorbing the cycle — same sweep, same idle bookkeeping, no cross-controller races. Interval is measured from the end of the last peek, and a hibernation teardown counts as a peek end since the count is fresh at destruction. Eligibility keys on 'no live view', which covers both a hibernated view and one never created, and naturally excludes the active service. Muted services still peek and quiet hours never pause peeks — mute means silence, never blindness.

nodes.label: Peek lifecycle and noteUnreadReport
nodes.rationale: Starts via views.ensure so the overlay invariant holds trivially (a peek never calls activate). Ends on the first unread report, detected through a late-bound ctx.noteUnreadReport because MainState.setRuntime deliberately no-ops on an unchanged count and cannot be the signal. Teardown sets hibernated exactly like the sweep's, so a boot-peeked tile shows as sleeping, which it is; only real activation clears the flag.

nodes.label: neverHibernate default flips to false
nodes.rationale: The all-true default existed precisely because hibernation was blind — every service was kept resident so badges would work. With Light Sleep, sleeping is safe, so sleeping becomes the norm and Keep Awake becomes the per-service opt-out it was always meant to be. Installs that wrote the key keep their choices because conf only persists written keys.

nodes.label: Stale-banner disabled guard
nodes.rationale: Planning-time code reading corrected the brainstorm: click-through already activates the originating service. The remaining gap is a banner clicked after its service was disabled — activating a disabled service leaves no rail tile, no view, an unrestorable active id — so the handler shows the window only.

nodes.label: Quiet hours (scheduled global mute)
nodes.rationale: The notification story had per-service mute, global mute, a throttle and the one-sound rule but no clock. Effective silence becomes globalMuted || quietNow; because shouldNotify and audioMuted are inverse-defined, one added input silences banners and page audio together, so 'mute means silence, never blindness' holds by construction and badges stay untouched. Chosen shape: one daily window + active days, over a single every-day window and weekday/weekend profiles.

nodes.label: quiet-hours-rules.ts
nodes.rationale: All functions take now: Date; nothing reads the clock itself. A crossing window belongs to the day it starts — the only attribution that never produces split half-nights. start === end is an empty window, not 24-hour quiet. Time math uses local date parts so a DST jump lands boundaries where the wall clock says, and a late-firing timer self-corrects because every fire recomputes from the current clock.

nodes.label: quietOverrideWindowStart (the macOS DND rule)
nodes.rationale: Unmuting mid-window wins until the next window starts. The engaged window's start timestamp is its identity, so one persisted field records the dismissed window and a restart mid-window stays dismissed. Muting manually just sets globalMuted, which rightly outlives the window.

nodes.label: QuietHoursController and the shared side-effects tail
nodes.rationale: Owns exactly one setTimeout armed to nextBoundary and disposes it on before-quit per the bounded-timers rule. A boundary fire runs the same side effects setGlobalMuted runs, extracted into one shared helper so the two cannot drift; no settings write happens on a boundary because engagement is computed, never stored. ShellState gains quietActive on the existing broadcast — no new IPC channel.
nodes.norm_label: quiethourscontroller and the shared side-effects tail

nodes.label: Summon hotkey (global shortcut)
nodes.rationale: A hub app earns its place by being one keypress away; nothing used globalShortcut before. Focused → hide, anything else → show and focus. Two behaviours come free: win.on('focus') already routes keyboard focus into the active service view, and the tray's Hide/Show label already rebuilds on show/hide. Accepted quirk: a focused fullscreen window is a no-op because hiding it strands an empty macOS desktop space.

nodes.label: SUMMON_COMBOS curated list
nodes.rationale: A curated list of four cross-platform-safe accelerators was chosen over a fixed combo and a free-form recorder. The list, the default and comboLabel live in src/shared/summon.ts so the settings select, normalization and main share one source; normalize() coerces any accelerator not in the list back to the default.

nodes.label: summonHotkeyOk (no silent failure)
nodes.rationale: globalShortcut.register returns false when another app owns the combo, so the result lands on a MainState public field (event-driven state, like switcherOpen) and rides the existing broadcast into ShellState; the settings row shows a pick-another-combo hint. apply() returns true when disabled — off is never a failure.

nodes.label: Banner → exact conversation
nodes.rationale: The site stays the source of truth for its own routing: Goetia never learns any service's conversation URLs or DOM, it either replays the site's own click handler or follows an href the recipe already held. Every failure mode degrades to exactly today's behaviour — activate the service.

nodes.label: Lane A — replay the page's own click
nodes.rationale: The shim discarded the onclick the site attaches, which is precisely its 'focus this thread' code. A preload-scoped registry capped at 20 holds instances and lives and dies with the page's JS context — the correct lifetime, since the handlers are page closures. Tampering is a non-issue: the page can already call its own handlers, and a replayed handler routing off-chat is contained by chatPaths snapback. Sites the shim reroutes from ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification never hold the instance and fall back to activation.
nodes.norm_label: lane a — replay the page's own click

nodes.label: Lane B — synthetic banners carry an href
nodes.rationale: synthFromRows already walks the unread thread row whose anchor is the conversation link, so returning href adds no DOM walking. An href survives view teardown — it is a URL, not live JS — so synthetic banners route correctly long after a peek view died. A payload carrying both lanes is treated as lane B: href wins because it works dead or alive.
nodes.norm_label: lane b — synthetic banners carry an href

nodes.label: resolveBannerClick decision table
nodes.rationale: Pure logic in lib/notification-click.ts with NotificationRouter as thin wiring. Correction 2026-08-17: navigate shipped first, but a cross-document loadURL on a live view reboots the SPA and raises the waking cover for a 1-2s thread switch — so a live view routes in-page by clicking the matching anchor and a dead view gets the URL as its wake load. Hrefs are validated against service origin + chatPaths prefix, and any failure downgrades to plain activate.

nodes.label: BANNER_GRACE_MS (the Light Sleep interaction)
nodes.rationale: Light Sleep destroys a peek view seconds after its first report — usually before the user can click the banner it just fired, which would kill lane A for exactly the sleeping-service case the feature exists for. Grace defers only the destruction: the peek still ends on its first report so the next due service peeks on schedule. The stamp decays naturally, and mute/quiet hours produce no banner hence no stamp.

nodes.label: Auto-banish unused services
nodes.rationale: Opt-in and off by default: auto-disabling services is consequential enough that the user opts in, and existing users would otherwise watch rarely-used services vanish within a day of updating. Silent — no toast, no banner, consistent with hibernation; the tile leaves the rail and Home's banished section is the record. Fully recoverable: the login partition stays intact.

nodes.label: lastUsedAt persisted wall clock
nodes.rationale: Time while Goetia is closed counts as unused, so after a week away unused services banish shortly after relaunch. A runtime-only clock was rejected because a daily app restart would mean a 24h threshold never fires. Stamped by activateService folded into the write rememberSurface already makes — no new write cadence — and stamped whether or not the feature is enabled, so enabling it later starts with real usage history. Only activation counts: banners, badges, unread reports and peeks never touch the clock.

nodes.label: shouldBanish (banish-rules.ts)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors shouldHibernate. Exempts the disabled, the active service, neverHibernate services (a kept-awake service is one the user pinned, never trimmed), the in-flight peek, and any unstamped clock. An earlier draft keyed on the runtime hibernated flag instead of neverHibernate and was dropped: a service that boots asleep has no view and never gets the flag until a peek tears one down, so with Light Sleep off the feature would silently never fire.

nodes.label: Auto-banish sweep step and applyDisabledChange
nodes.rationale: Runs inside the existing HibernationController.sweep after the hibernate step rather than as a separate BanishController, which would duplicate the sweep timer, boot delay, disposal and peek-awareness for a check sharing all of hibernation's inputs. Missing clocks are seeded at the first enabled sweep so migration, newly-enabled services and toggling on each grant a fresh window. All due services land in ONE patch through applyDisabledChange, which lives in ipc-handlers.ts because it calls buildAppMenu (electron) and would poison activate.ts's electron-free import graph; the sweep reaches it through late-bound ctx.banishServices. A sweep that banished skips peek scheduling because its settings snapshot is stale.

nodes.label: Sleep settings move to the Services pane
nodes.rationale: Hibernate-after-minutes, Light Sleep and Battery saver are all about sleeping services and read oddly split across two panes; General keeps close-to-tray, launch-at-login and the summoning hotkey.
nodes.norm_label: sleep settings move to the services pane

nodes.label: Home board ↔ rail reorder sync
nodes.rationale: The board seeds staged from the live order but reseeds on membership only, so a rail drop while Home is open left staged stale: 'Apply new order' lit up untouched and would commit the stale order, silently undoing the rail drag that lit it. Renderer-only — no main or IPC changes.

nodes.label: followLiveOrder (clean board follows silently)
nodes.rationale: When the board is clean, staged resyncs to the live summoned join and the confirm button stays 'No changes'. Dirty boards are never clobbered: with the modal in place the only way the live order changes under a dirty board is the user confirming the discard, which cleans it first.

nodes.label: RailReorderPrompt modal
nodes.rationale: A modal over a toast is a deliberate exception to the usual non-blocking-UI preference: the staged edit can carry summons and banishes, and losing it to a stray drag is exactly the surprise the modal exists to prevent. Silent last-write-wins and blocking rail drags were both rejected — the latter hides why nothing moves. Escape and backdrop mean Keep editing, with the listener in the capture phase so Welcome's own Escape-closes-Home handler never fires underneath.

nodes.label: useTileReorder commit intercept
nodes.rationale: An optional intercept called at drag end with the merged orderedIds — returning true defers the commit (draft kept, nothing sent) — plus a cancelDraft() for the snap-back. Reorder still reaches IPC at most once per drag, now possibly deferred behind the modal decision; the draft clears when the broadcast lands, so the drop never snaps back for a frame.

nodes.label: homeDirty / discardHomeDraft store fields
nodes.rationale: Welcome↔Rail coordination that never leaves the renderer: homeDirty is published from the existing orderChanged (which already covers adds, removals and order) and cleared on unmount; discardHomeDraft is a bumped tick Welcome subscribes to.

nodes.label: Login purge (rename of sign out)
nodes.rationale: 'Sign out…' over-promised: the server session is never revoked, so the site keeps listing the device until the token expires. The word is replaced in copy, in the IPC channel and in the module name at the same time so label and code cannot drift the way they just did. 'Purge' was chosen over 'forget' and 'clear session' — goetic verb with a plain object, and the bulk button reads as the heavier sibling of the per-service one.

nodes.label: Purge and banish are orthogonal axes
nodes.rationale: Banish clears the rail and keeps the login; purge clears the login and never touches disabled or order, so a purge-all leaves the board exactly as the user arranged it. Purging as part of banish was rejected: it conflates the two axes and would make the rail a destructive control.
nodes.norm_label: purge and banish are orthogonal axes

nodes.label: confirmPurgeAll (Home-wide sweep)
nodes.rationale: Settings lists enabled services only, so a banished service's credentials sat on disk with no UI that could touch them — the sweep covers every service in order, summoned and unbound, which is the point. Invoke rather than send because the dialog is modal and the wipes are async: the renderer awaits the count and owns the toast, so nothing is added to ShellState and no broadcast is needed for a one-shot acknowledgement. registerInvoke widens its handler type to allow a promise.

nodes.label: Acknowledgement checkbox re-prompt loop
nodes.rationale: showMessageBox returns checkboxChecked only after a button press, so a native dialog cannot gate a button on the box; confirming unticked re-shows the dialog once with a nudge line and unticked on the second pass cancels. Staying native keeps Home's confirm consistent with Settings' per-service one and costs no new shell surface — a renderer-side modal would truly disable the button but needs its own surface and tests.

nodes.label: purgeService shared unit
nodes.rationale: Closes call windows first because the dialog promises the call ends and a call window runs in the partition being cleared; clears persist:<id> storage; loadServiceUrl is already a no-op with no view, which is what makes the same unit work for hibernated and unbound services; zeroes the runtime unread because a hibernated service would otherwise keep a badge for messages the user can no longer open; and clears the service's ActivityLog entries because recents rows are titles from the session just wiped and would deep-link to a login page.

nodes.label: --danger color token
nodes.rationale: Deliberately in --badge's pink-red family rather than the ember accent's: a destructive control must not read as brand orange, and --accent is too close to warn-orange to carry 'this deletes things'. --badge itself means unread and reusing it would conflate an unread count with a destructive action; --accent-2 is the end stop of the hero's summon gradient, so repurposing it would make that gradient read as a warning.

nodes.label: PurgeToast (bottom-centre slot)
nodes.rationale: For a purely unbound service nothing else on screen changes, so silence would leave the user unsure the sweep ran. Driven by renderer-local store state rather than ShellState, which would make a one-shot acknowledgement part of every subsequent broadcast. Bottom-centre because UpdateToast holds bottom-right and CapTrimToast bottom-left and the two can overlap — the centre needs no conditional offsets or coupling.

nodes.label: Sign-out moves to Settings → Services
nodes.rationale: It is a destructive-rare action and belongs with the service's other controls, not one mis-click away on a tile. The new service:signOut channel is shell-only — a service page must never trigger a partition wipe, its own included — and gets its own named sender-policy test because a partition wipe is exactly the channel whose classification deserves one.

nodes.label: Banish on the tile menu
nodes.rationale: Tile menu = Mute/Unmute + separator + Banish. Banish is quick and fully recoverable — the login partition is kept and the service waits in Home's banished section — so it gets no confirm; a dialog would defeat 'quick'. It reuses ctx.banishServices, the same one-patch disable through applyDisabledChange, and banishing the active service is already handled by resolveActivation and the all-disabled derivation.

nodes.label: Matches ranked first, other services still listed
nodes.norm_label: matches ranked first, other services still listed

nodes.label: Accelerators track rail order, not filtered position
nodes.norm_label: accelerators track rail order, not filtered position

nodes.label: Mute Silences But Never Hides Badges
nodes.norm_label: mute silences but never hides badges

nodes.label: Settings Has No Service Enable Toggle
nodes.norm_label: settings has no service enable toggle
