nodes.label: Ad-hoc Signature Consequences
nodes.rationale: Every build's ad-hoc signature has its own cdhash as designated requirement, so macOS sees a new app identity per rebuild — hence the Goetia Safe Storage keychain re-prompt after every update, and why platform passkey authenticators (Team-ID entitlements) are unavailable. Permanent fix is a paid signing identity.

nodes.label: Ember Portal Branding
nodes.rationale: The icon is a summoning circle as pure energy, matching the ember accent (dark #FF9E2C, light #E8590C); SVG sources in resources/, PNGs regenerated with rsvg-convert.

nodes.label: Software Authenticator
nodes.rationale: User decision 2026-08-30: a software authenticator in main behind a preload shim, because Electron's Touch ID authenticator needs a Team-ID entitlement ad-hoc signing cannot honour, Apple lets only real browsers assert iCloud passkeys, and CDP virtual authenticators disable background throttling 24/7. Same model as 1Password/Bitwarden shimming navigator.credentials.

nodes.label: WebAuthn Shim (webauthn-shim.ts)
nodes.rationale: Preload patches navigator.credentials.create/get for publicKey requests only, forwards over serviceId-validated invoke channels, builds returned credentials with the native PublicKeyCredential prototype so instanceof passes, honours AbortSignal. All it can do is ask — private keys never leave main.

nodes.label: PasskeyAuthenticator (Ceremony Owner)
nodes.rationale: Main owns the ceremony: validate rpId against the origin from e.senderFrame.url (never the payload), verify the user (Touch ID else native confirm), sign. The only code that decrypts a key, for one signature. One in-flight ceremony per view, WEBAUTHN_TIMEOUT_MS cap.

nodes.label: PasskeyStore (passkeys.json)
nodes.rationale: One store keyed by rpId shared across services — safe because rpId binds to the frame origin, not the partition; a facebook.com passkey made in Messenger serves Instagram. Private keys safeStorage-encrypted; PASSKEY_CAP 50; forget with one-step restore; survives purge and banish because a passkey is a credential, not a session.

nodes.label: rpId Registrable-Suffix Validation
nodes.rationale: rpId must equal the origin host or be a dot-suffix with at least two labels; no public-suffix list is needed while every reachable host is in ALLOWED_HOSTS and none sits under a multi-label public suffix — which is why 'Adding a service' gained the no-shared-suffix rule.

nodes.label: UV Set on Accepted Confirm
nodes.rationale: UV is set whether verification was Touch ID or a click on a machine without it — setting UV only for real biometrics would make Microsoft (userVerification: required) reject every Windows sign-in; 1Password/Bitwarden count unlocked-vault-plus-click as verification, and the unlocked OS session is the equivalent boundary.

nodes.label: Passkey Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Four accepted weaknesses: click-as-verification without Touch ID; safeStorage keys extractable by same-user malware (Secure Enclave is the paid upgrade); sign counter 0 means no clone detection (as synced passkeys); rpId without a PSL, mitigated by the ALLOWED_HOSTS rule. None widens reach beyond what cookie theft already allows.

nodes.label: encodeCbor (Canonical CBOR Encoder)
nodes.rationale: Minimal RFC 8949 slice an authenticator emits — ints, byte/text strings, arrays, maps in CTAP2 canonical key order; floats/tags throw rather than encode wrongly. No new dependency.

nodes.label: WebAuthn Wire Types (shared/webauthn.ts)
nodes.rationale: Process-agnostic wire shapes between shim and main; every BufferSource travels as base64url, matching WebAuthn's own JSON serialization; fromBase64Url returns null instead of throwing so callers map to the right WebAuthn error.

nodes.label: webauthn-crypto (Keys, authData, Signatures)
nodes.rationale: P-256 key generation, COSE/SPKI dual export, clientDataJSON, authenticatorData layout (rpIdHash ‖ flags ‖ counter 0 ‖ attested data), none-attestation object, DER ECDSA assertion signatures over authData ‖ sha256(clientDataJSON).

nodes.label: webauthn-rules (Request Validation)
nodes.rationale: rpIdAllowed, hostOfOrigin (https only — only https pages hold a session worth a passkey), parseCreation/parseAssertion mapping every failure to the DOMException name pages branch on.

nodes.label: Recipe.loginUrl Hook
nodes.rationale: User decision 2026-08-30, deliberately reopening two prior rejections (2026-08-12 loginRedirect, 2026-08-13 firstRunUrl teardown): a recipe may declare a login URL only for a logged-OUT shell with no sign-in form in sight. Fires once per document, page-initiated via location.assign so will-navigate containment still sees it, shares the snap-back floor. Slack keeps starting on url because its logged-out page already is a form.

nodes.label: TikTok Logged-out Shell
nodes.rationale: Signed out, TikTok's /messages renders the feed nav rail plus an empty DM drawer and a small Log in button — no sign-in form (live capture 2026-08-29). Detected by top-login-button present AND top-dm-icon absent; the /login page renders neither hook so the result is null there by construction.

nodes.label: Identity Popup (Hardened Sign-in Window)
nodes.rationale: A window.open matching isIdentityPopup opens as a visible hardened popup (isolated, sandboxed, same persist:<id>) that keeps window.opener because the callback finishes through postMessage. No adoption — severing the opener kills completion. Safe where the call popup was not: it opens on a real https URL so the webPreferences override applies, and a sandboxed popup cannot share the unsandboxed view's process.

nodes.label: IDENTITY_PROVIDERS Table
nodes.rationale: Global provider table (user decision) — the popup is hardened regardless of opener, so per-service declarations would add editing for no safety gain. Entry paths gate only the opening URL; grown only from live-pass evidence and [nav] popup denied: audit lines, never from memory. IdP hosts never enter ALLOWED_HOSTS.

nodes.label: ROAMING_HOSTS
nodes.rationale: Live-pass finding 2026-08-31: Facebook's SDK finishes through the staticxx.facebook.com xd_arbiter, a host isIdentityHost refused, so the popup could never complete. ROAMING_HOSTS lists mid-flow hosts that are never an entry; isIdentityHost consults it, isIdentityPopup still refuses them.

nodes.label: Pre-commit will-redirect Hand-back
nodes.rationale: The contained window hands a login back on will-redirect before the callback commits, so the one-time OAuth code is consumed exactly once and sessionStorage-stashed PKCE/state survives. Never will-navigate — it may carry a POST body Electron does not expose (Apple's form_post), so a prevented POST would hand back an empty GET.

nodes.label: Google Secure-Browser Block
nodes.rationale: Google refuses OAuth in embedded browsers server-side, after email submit — UA string, Sec-CH-UA headers and navigator.userAgentData were all spoofed correctly and it still blocked. The userAgentData preload was reverted (user decision 2026-08-31): contextIsolation:false on a page talking to a real IdP is a real hardening cost that bought nothing. Google login is left to email/password or another provider; Insomnia-style system-browser flows don't apply because the service, not Goetia, is the OAuth client.

nodes.label: Client-Hint Header Injection
nodes.rationale: Electron sends no Sec-CH-UA at all — a Chrome UA with zero hint headers is itself the embedded-browser tell. lib/client-hints.ts builds the three low-entropy hints with a Google Chrome brand, injected via onBeforeSendHeaders scoped to identity hosts only. Kept after the Google block persisted, because they are correct Chrome behaviour and harmless.

nodes.label: Popup vs Redirect OAuth Flows
nodes.rationale: Redirect flows (Slack, Instagram) already worked through the contained window; popup flows (Google Identity Services, FB.login, Sign in with Apple JS) finish via window.opener.postMessage and have no redirect fallback, so the OS browser — different cookie jar, no opener — could never complete them. This distinction is why the identity popup exists.

nodes.label: hostMatches (Shared Suffix Matcher)
nodes.rationale: Exact or .suffix host match shared by navigation-policy and identity-policy so both spell suffixes the same way; .slack.com matches slack.com and subdomains, never evilslack.com which bare endsWith would admit.

nodes.label: IdentityShare (Cookie Seeding Unit)
nodes.rationale: Lends persist:messenger's facebook.com cookies to a Continue-with-Facebook popup for the popup's lifetime only — seed on create, unseed on close plus IDENTITY_SEED_GRACE_MS (10s, sized for the arbiter round trip, deliberately not BANNER_GRACE_MS). The whole cookie set moves including datr/sb fingerprint cookies, or a known session with an unknown fingerprint triggers a new-device checkpoint. Cookie values never cross IPC, never touch a Goetia file, never get logged.

nodes.label: FB_APP_IDS Gate
nodes.rationale: Seeding requires the dialog's client_id/app_id to match a value captured from a live sign-in (ships empty, never filled from memory). It carries the security: a malicious/XSS'd page opening its own dialog/oauth against a seeded jar would collect a token on one click, and the popup guard cannot contain that because the SDK answers by postMessage through the staticxx arbiter, never navigating anywhere refusable. It refuses a stranger's app but NOT the site's own app turned against the user — which is why local verification also exists.

nodes.label: IDENTITY_SOURCE (persist:messenger)
nodes.rationale: Messenger's URL is www.facebook.com/messages/, so its partition holds the Facebook session by construction — derived from SERVICES rather than spelled 'messenger', with a test pinning the derivation. Zero new persisted session state; Purge Messenger already means log out of Facebook everywhere.

nodes.label: Identity-Share Local Verification (Touch ID)
nodes.rationale: User decision 2026-09-02: Touch ID (else a native confirm, the passkey prompt's fallback reused) before every seed — deliberately not a passkey and not WebAuthn, just local verification before a credential crosses partitions. Exists because FB_APP_IDS closes only half the escalation; asked only after rules 5-6 so a popup that would not be seeded never prompts. Remembering the answer per service was rejected: the one service an XSS would target is precisely the one already approved.

nodes.label: shouldSeed Six Rules
nodes.rationale: Toggle on; URL is a Facebook dialog; app id matches FB_APP_IDS[target]; target is not the source; source jar has a live session (c_user); target jar has none. Rule 6 leaves Instagram's own Log-in-with-Facebook cookies alone and makes deliberate second-account logins sticky. maySeed (rules 1-4) is split out because the sync gate must decide before the first await — a stopped popup is blank until re-navigated.

nodes.label: Stop-Seed-Replay Popup Timing
nodes.rationale: setWindowOpenHandler is sync and every cookie API is async, so there is no window to seed before the first request leaves. seedIdentityPopup stops the popup's load, seeds, and replays with httpReferrer — deterministic, and re-navigating the same WebContents keeps window.opener because opener is a property of the browsing context, not the document. The Sec-Fetch-Site risk closed on the 2026-09-02 live pass; plan B (header injection) stays unbuilt.

nodes.label: identity-seeds.json Crash Marker
nodes.rationale: Durable marker holding seeded service ids (never a cookie value), written before the first cookies.set, swept at startup — a crash with a popup open must not strand a lent session. A blanket boot strip was rejected because it would destroy the deliberate second-account logins rule 6 protects. unseed verifies the jar is clean before unmarking, because cookies.remove reports a URL matching nothing by doing nothing — unmarking on faith would strand a live session AND hide it from the sweep.

nodes.label: sanitizeBanner
nodes.rationale: Banner text is page-controlled and typed only by convention — a shim can be bypassed — so main re-coerces non-strings to '' and clamps title/body (200/500) before any use. Closes the new Notification(null) main-process crash (audit S4 + M8).

nodes.label: IPC Handler Crash-Proofing
nodes.rationale: try/catch inside register()/registerInvoke so a page-shaped payload can never throw out of an ipcMain listener and kill main; e.senderFrame reads move inside the try because a disposed frame throws on property access.

nodes.label: Display-Media Confirm Fallback
nodes.rationale: Audit S1: the non-system-picker fallback handed sources[0] — the whole primary screen — to the page with zero interaction. Replaced with a native confirm naming the service; deny on cancel or error, so getDisplayMedia() from a compromised page costs a visible, named confirm.

nodes.label: facebookAppId Param-Pollution Refusal
nodes.rationale: Audit S2: Facebook's backend reads the LAST duplicate param while URLSearchParams.get() reads the first — a polluted URL could seed one app and render another — so facebookAppId returns null unless exactly one id exists across client_id/app_id; seedable dialogs additionally require the versionless /dialog/oauth path and a redirect_uri, so /login stays open-able but never seedable.

nodes.label: Hash-aware chatPaths
nodes.rationale: Teams routes every surface off one pathname (/v2/#/chat vs #/calendar), so the runner matches prefixes against pathname + hash; pathname-only recipes are untouched because hash is '' for them. The hash in the service URL makes snapback a free same-document fragment navigation — no reload, no boot splash.

nodes.label: webauthn-block.ts (Superseded)
nodes.rationale: Found during the first Teams live login 2026-08-13: Microsoft's passkey-first sign-in parked forever because Electron had no platform authenticator, so the block deleted PublicKeyCredential and rejected passkey requests with NotSupportedError — sites feature-detect no support and offer a password. Superseded 2026-08-30 by the software authenticator.

nodes.label: Wake Captions Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Seven tasks: LoadKind type + wakeCaption helper, defaultRuntime wakeKind null, MainLoads carries the kind, WakingTracker.begin records it, wiring through views.ts/index.ts/loading overlay, ContentPlaceholder keyed on waking, CLAUDE.md guardrail. Commits are never made by agents in this repo.

nodes.label: Wake Captions Design Spec
nodes.rationale: Two fixes to one phrase: the cover over-claimed 'Waking' for every main-requested load (⌘R, crash restart, purge, login hand-back), and ContentPlaceholder was keyed on runtime.loading (did-start-loading, fired by any subframe fetch) so a live Discord read 'Waking Discord…' behind ⌘K. The kind rides the existing MainLoads mark so no new event or channel is needed.

nodes.label: Five load kinds (wake, reload, restart, purge, hand-back)
nodes.rationale: Five kinds cover the seven views.load callers. Any view creation is a wake (user decision 2026-09-05): a hibernation wake and a dead-view open are the view built from nothing, like a cold create; 'Resuming' for hibernation wakes was rejected as a distinction the user cannot see. The crash placeholder's Retry is a reload (user pressed it, goes through views.refresh); restart is reserved for the app's own post-crash reload.
nodes.norm_label: five load kinds (wake, reload, restart, purge, hand-back)

nodes.label: ContentPlaceholder keyed on waking, not loading
nodes.rationale: runtime.loading is did-start-loading, which fires for any subframe or page-initiated load, so a fully rendered Discord read 'Waking Discord…' behind the switcher the moment it fetched anything. The cover never had this problem because it is keyed on waking. runtime.loading keeps its meaning but stops driving user-facing text.
nodes.norm_label: contentplaceholder keyed on waking, not loading

nodes.label: null wakeKind renders the wake caption
nodes.rationale: wakeKind may be null while waking is true only if a future begin() caller forgets the kind; the helper treats null as wake so the cover never renders an empty caption. end() leaves wakeKind as it was because nothing reads it while waking is false.
nodes.norm_label: null wakekind renders the wake caption

nodes.label: Slack thread open design
nodes.rationale: Accepted 2026-09-05: a pin captured in a thread and a recents row for a thread reply open the thread in the flexpane instead of the channel.

nodes.label: Canonical Slack thread URL
nodes.rationale: https://app.slack.com/client/<T>/<C>/thread/<C>-<ts>. Approach A of three: a structured handle field was rejected as a new schema in four places; encoding the thread into the conversation label was rejected as corrupting a user-visible string. Same-origin, so pin-rules, pins.json and the origin check are untouched; workspace-host archives permalinks are never a pin form.

nodes.label: The flexpane rule
nodes.rationale: conversationUrl returns null when a non-empty selection's anchor node is outside [data-qa=threads_flexpane], so a selection in the channel pane while a thread is open pins the channel.

nodes.label: The url lane in openConversationInPage
nodes.rationale: Between same and anchor: opts.byUrl(doc, req.url) wired to recipe.openUrl; true returns 'url', false or a throw moves on. Runs only with a validated url so an unvalidated href never reaches a recipe. Worst case is unchanged: every miss ends in the load lane and the channel.

nodes.label: Recents learn rule (learnedUrl)
nodes.rationale: Learn when the report equals the document URL, or when it validates like a click-time href and differs from where the document was. Accepting a page-controlled report grants nothing new: learned URLs re-validate on every click, and the page could already navigate there during replay.

nodes.label: Dead-view limit
nodes.rationale: A pin opened while Slack's view is gone is still a navigate action; Slack boots into the channel and drops the thread. Re-running the in-page open after wake is a recorded follow-up.

nodes.label: Discord thread addendum (2026-09-06)
nodes.rationale: Discord threads have no anchor anywhere: split form opens by clicking the parent channel then #message-accessories-<thread>; full-window form by clicking [data-list-item-id=channels___<id>]; last resort is pushState + synthetic popstate trusted only once [id^=chat-messages-<id>-] renders, else history.back() and the load lane.

nodes.label: conversationUrl / openUrl hook pair
nodes.rationale: Two optional Recipe hooks declared together; recipes.test.ts enforces that a recipe declaring one declares the other.

nodes.label: Slack thread open implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Five tasks: hook types + fixture + slackThreadUrl; openSlackThread; the url lane and OpenLane; preload/main wiring with learnedUrl; docs and live pass. Lane order replay > name > same > url > anchor > load.

nodes.label: tests/fixtures/slack-thread.html
nodes.rationale: Trimmed from the 2026-09-05 live snapshot: sidebar rows, channel pane with root message and reply bar, flexpane with root. The oracle for both hooks.

nodes.label: Passkey setup page (REJECTED)
nodes.rationale: Built and driven live 2026-09-08, then rejected on principle: loading Microsoft's account-security page into the Teams view made the user operate a non-chat site inside a chat app. Part 2 removed before commit; do not revive as a Settings entry, notice button or recipe hook.

nodes.label: Microsoft passkey-first dead end
nodes.rationale: The shim advertises a platform authenticator everywhere, so Microsoft goes passkey-first, Goetia finds nothing for login.microsoft.com, and the user lands on a page with Back and a disabled Try again. Fix shipped: wording in noPasskey — Back > Other ways to sign in > password.

nodes.label: Keep advertising the authenticator everywhere
nodes.rationale: Answering 'no authenticator' per site would send Microsoft to the password but nearly every site gates its create-a-passkey offer on the same check, so organic creation would stop for all services.

nodes.label: The chat-only exception (withdrawn)
nodes.rationale: Proposed justification for loading a non-chat page: it manages the credential for the chat, reached only from Settings, returns on its own. Withdrawn with the rejection.

nodes.label: App lock
nodes.rationale: Opt-in lock screen in front of the whole app, engaged at launch and on demand, released by Touch ID or a Goetia passcode. One lock for the whole app (per-service would leave banners, pins, recents open); no idle timer or lock-on-hide.

nodes.label: Threat model: a screen guard, not encryption
nodes.rationale: Defends against a person with physical access to the unlocked machine; not against anyone who can read the profile or run a process as the user (cookies decrypt via the login keychain). Removing lock.json turns it off — a deliberate, documented escape hatch. A locked Goetia is still online.
nodes.norm_label: threat model: a screen guard, not encryption

nodes.label: Touch ID authenticates any enrolled finger
nodes.rationale: Up to five fingers, often a partner's; against that person Touch ID is not a lock. Hence Touch ID is separately switchable (on by default) and every configuration change requires the passcode, never Touch ID.
nodes.norm_label: touch id authenticates any enrolled finger

nodes.label: A native confirm is consent, not authentication
nodes.rationale: The passkey prompt's showMessageBox fallback has an OK anyone can click; an app lock must not accept it. Same reason a native-prompt-only lock with no surface was rejected.
nodes.norm_label: a native confirm is consent, not authentication

nodes.label: locked joins anyOverlayOpen
nodes.rationale: Approach A of three: a lock screen is precisely a shell surface a service view would cover. presentSurface hides every view, pin-selection becomes a no-op, devtools targets the shell. Views stay warm and hidden so badges count and the last service is instant at unlock. A separate always-on-top window was rejected (one long-lived window assumption).

nodes.label: runShellCommand returns early while locked
nodes.rationale: The single funnel menu items and the in-view interceptor share; without it View > Toggle Developer Tools is a one-click bypass and Cmd-1 puts a service on screen. Greying is legibility; the guard is the enforcement.

nodes.label: LOCKED_ALLOWED_CHANNELS
nodes.rationale: Content-serving shell channels refuse while locked, structurally in the register() wrapper; only lock:unlock, lock:configure and badge:overlay are served. Service channels are untouched — refusing service:ready would strand a wake cover.

nodes.label: Redacted broadcast while locked
nodes.rationale: ShellState.pins goes out as []; counts, metadata, theme and settings still do, so even devtools on the shell shows no message text.

nodes.label: The waking cover obeys anyOverlayOpen (fourth gate)
nodes.rationale: Found in implementation: loading.html is a third view above the shell and syncOverlay hand-tested the three flags, painting 'Waking Zalo…' over the lock screen. The focus handler and startup views.activate had drifted the same way; all now read anyOverlayOpen.

nodes.label: Passcode as scrypt hash in safeStorage-encrypted lock.json
nodes.rationale: Minimum six characters, no composition rules — rate limiting is what makes a local secret survive guessing. Hashing matters beyond safeStorage because it protects against another user, not a process running as this one, and passcodes are reused. Never in settings.json, which is broadcast raw.
nodes.norm_label: passcode as scrypt hash in safestorage-encrypted lock.json

nodes.label: An unreadable credential fails closed
nodes.rationale: A credential that will not decrypt (denied keychain, copied profile) must not read as 'no passcode', which would silently open the app; the lock screen names the lock.json removal.

nodes.label: Failed-attempt backoff
nodes.rationale: 1s, 2s, 4s… capped at 30s, in memory, reset on success. No permanent lockout or wipe — both punish the owner more than an attacker who can walk away. The backoff is checked before the credential, so the first attempt after a failure is refused on time even if correct.

nodes.label: Configuration requires the passcode, never Touch ID
nodes.rationale: Unlocking may use either door; enabling, disabling, changing the passcode and toggling Touch ID accept only the passcode, because the credential a second enrolled finger defeats must not widen or remove the lock it guards.
nodes.norm_label: configuration requires the passcode, never touch id

nodes.label: Lock screen asks which door
nodes.rationale: User decision 2026-09-13: with both doors open, two buttons (Use Touch ID / Enter passcode) and nothing auto-prompted; the first cut stacked field, button, link and the macOS sheet. With Touch ID off or absent the passcode field is the screen.

nodes.label: Banners are redacted while locked, never suppressed
nodes.rationale: Silence would cost the ping that says come back; full banners would show sender and message. Title becomes the service name, body emptied; sound and throttling unchanged; the activity log keeps the real title.
nodes.norm_label: banners are redacted while locked, never suppressed

nodes.label: Parked banner click
nodes.rationale: A banner click while locked must not run performBannerAction (a one-click bypass); it shows the window and parks {serviceId, entryId} in one slot, replayed through resolveBannerClick on unlock so re-validation happens at click time. Last write wins, cleared on lock.
